entries.source: When work becomes too laborious, a strange whale comes to relax the Queen of Waves.
Some marine species have supposedly mutated just to enjoy the works of art on the surface.
The Oniyx? Serious as ever… but only when it comes to work. Like the Inventor, if disturbed, he growls in hexadecimal.
Lisa can do everything—except cook a meal. Faced with disaster, Frost forbids her from entering the kitchen.
Before being King and Queen, light and shadow were just two childhood friends who grew up together before parting ways.
In the north of Emeldarion, a cereal grows by pyrosynthesis: the Bleh. This land is ideal for pyromaniacs looking to turn to farming.
Dragons are intelligent and majestic creatures, yet capable of sulking for two centuries just because someone told them “no.”
On Aelther, the pilgrim walking the sacred paths survives by feeding on caterpillars, juicy and honeyed.
The sage on a sacred stone adds an unnecessary step to the pilgrimage, just to admire the pilgrims’ reactions.
Exiled by the construction of Dragheir, the ancient ice penguins now live near lava, forever dreaming of their homeland.
Gabriel and Lumisaros? Two brilliant friends who theorized about the perfect chair… after long reflection, they work standing up, on principle.
The beauty of black coral described in stories is, in truth, nothing but the sight of gaspoison deposits at the bottom of the sea.
A chef compiles his frog-based recipes with rigor. In the marshes, one can hear him with a sharp and resounding “Croac Croac.”
Heraldesse is a telepath… often found drunk due to the backlash of her intoxicating powers. Telepathy must be practiced in moderation.
The octoflora knocks out its visitors… then recycles them into fertilizer, a solution to climate change.
Great lions know how to read. One of them is preparing a novel for the coming winter—if only he knew how to write.
Do not confuse a proper name with an event: Aurelia is not called Aurora.
The Primordial Codex? Shattered into a thousand pieces, simply because Nebula was too curious.
Slaying an abyssal creature releases a strange black smoke… smoking kills!
To avoid elemental imbalance and keep a sane mind, it is recommended to exhaust 5 spells or incantations per day.
Zayd must eat on schedule, otherwise he starts chewing whatever lies around.
The Master of Hues never dreams… but he paints his nightmares.
Those nightmares materialize in the real world as abyssal monsters.
The pyramids of Shal’Zaar once produced electricity, but all stopped the day they collapsed.
The world created by the deities is a perfect sphere—who would ever believe in a flat one?
Vladislaus once got lost in his own manor of shifting rooms. He no longer leaves his living room, and Bernard, his butler, tends to him.
The burning willow is the only creature capable of resisting elemental corruption by purifying its habitat.
The Natus are wild and territorial, organized into tribes with different cultures depending on their environment.
The Alphilans are fish-men who despise surface creatures, especially since the disappearance of their king.
The Infernal City once used the flows of Mount Vulcain to forge the finest materials.
The ancient magical runes have lost their power, but they remain sacred to pilgrims.
Mages must train their entire lives to strengthen their magic, using rare and precious catalysts.
The TOX enhance an individual’s abilities, but they can cause dependency and dangerous side effects.
The nation of shadow is represented by the eye of the observer—always vigilant, always hidden.
The nation of light is associated with the ear of the hunter, ever loyal even in the face of voices from the shadow.
The nation of nature is tied to the palm of the healer, gentle and attentive to every life.
The nation of fire carries the fists of the worker, strong, relentless, always in motion.
The nation of water is represented by the mouth of the negotiator, fluid and persuasive.
The nation of earth is linked to the nose of the seeker, able to sense the secrets buried beneath the rock.
The Pack is a cult dedicated to Aeltheria, dwelling in the northeast of Emeldarion.

Elther would not exist without the Deities: all living things are the product of divine creation. Aeltheria is the creator of every Deity. Her favored form is said to be that of a she-wolf, making the animal a sacred and deeply revered figure throughout Elther. On the day of the Great Cataclysm, the Awakened peoples joined forces to seal away the Deities; the creature they imprisoned had the form of a gigantic she-wolf. Many theories exist, but all draw a connection to Aeltheria. Faerylia is being actively sought, as she may hold answers on the matter.

The history lessons at the Dragheïr military school often speak of Aidan. Child of the heir to the Fire runic weapon, he followed proudly in his father's footsteps. A master of his own martial arts, he was also fluent in the Dhöggeïr language. His abilities were recorded, and they now serve as the foundation for training their soldiers. Today, at his father's side, Aidan dwells in the Infernal City as a humanoid Abyssal. Lisa often speaks of her dreams, in which she becomes Aidan in his past everyday life — but also, at times, in his present suffering.

They say six children were born with a rune on their hand. In Lumethia, not far from the sacred sage's stone, a noble family thirsting for adventure gave birth to Gorakar. This family long dreamed of adventure until the day their dream called them to make a pilgrimage. Summoned to the heart of the Lonely Isles, the young adventurer set off to join Aldrin. His parents, on a different journey, then called upon the most erudite of the Tokscyth. With his revolutionary flying machine, they will set off to meet a powerful Dhöggeïr at the heart of the flying islands.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, which nightmares then purify. Some corrupted souls nevertheless retain their memories and exploit dream rifts to possess living creatures. Nightmare-Eaters evade the Nightmare Reaper by posing as friends to their prey. Once possession is complete, they mutate their victim until they have seized total control. This scourge is so notorious in Nyevielh that the tale of Aleera, the corrupted little girl, has spread to every household.

The great military fortress-city of Dragheïr is a dam between the ocean and the Blazing Sea, a place of exchange between Eltherians and Dhöggeïrs, and a city rich in symbols with a noble martial culture. Amber is one of those symbols: a female warrior who masters Water and Fire and represents the alliance between Hadeïr and Nordvinter. Legend says that one day, two heroes who oppose each other in every way will manage to free Hadeïr from the flames. They will purify Mount Vulcan and free the mother of the Dhöggeïr. Amber is a charismatic, combative figure.

Originally from the Lonely Isles, an anthropomorphic martial master carrying a magical artifact settled northwest of Emeldarion. One day, his unattended staff was used on a mushroom. The magic took effect, and the fungus assumed a humanoid form. Because it constantly demanded bitter flavors, many believed it was saying that its name was Ameru; the name stuck. Grateful for this second life, the new morphic being introduced unusual addictive crops that became wildly popular in Abondance. This new form of agriculture allowed the Water shamans to prosper.

Originally from the Lonely Isles, an anthropomorphic martial master carrying a magical artifact settled northwest of Emeldarion. With that artifact, Amphibian brought many inhabitants of the Water shaman village to life. In time, his most gifted students surpassed him. He therefore organized a succession tournament with one simple rule: “The winner receives the morphic staff.” The Apprentice Evoker, determined to transform his family into Anthropomorphs, prevailed and became the tribe’s new leader. He then ordered the construction of watering places suited to new animal species.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, which nightmares then purify. Eternal agents patrol the Abyss with a divine task of macabre cleansing. The one called Nightmare Reaper regulates the overpopulation of nightmares that cannot find inner peace, cutting short their very existence, which is harmful to the cycle imposed by the divinities.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, which nightmares then purify. Eternal agents patrol the Abyss to keep their shifting state stable. The one called Nebular Aristocrat mends the dream-rifts between the two worlds. With perfect mastery of the divine runes, she weaves the border between worlds.

The world really needs a researcher, a true one — the greatest of all the Tokscyth and, objectively, the most handsome. The Artisan of Hours is an unrivalled inventor and a traveler who observes the world and records all his adventures in a single book. Originally from Lumethia, he built a superb flying machine that will let him reach the heart of the Lonely Isles. This dream of exploration allows him to perfect his already flawless knowledge.

When the Water Spirit began its regulatory mission, Lycaria noticed the overpopulation around the spirit's lake. In Nordvinter, while the Spirit held back the advance of the Crystal Lands, the Eternal took on a form combining Anthropomorph and Pixarch traits, with runes engraved on her body. Her aura recalls her closeness to the divine will. She makes sure no one abuses her leniency. She seeks to preserve the tranquility of the lake and its surroundings.

Spatiotemporal displacements are rarely witnessed. Young Astry creates rifts similar to Vivy's. He appears alone on the beaches of Aelther, far from the pilgrim paths. We were lucky enough to hear him say his own name while talking to himself. He seems to stay around the western coasts, where he fights abyssal monsters emerging from the Starry Sea. His supernatural powers and spectacular battles leave onlookers speechless. His apparent youth and his powers raise questions about his origin. No one dares disturb him, following the directives imposed on the continent of Aelther.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. Pods of unusual cetaceans migrate from the Ocean of the Depths. Prankster Whales delight in teasing Lumethian ships, often greeting them by pretending to capsize them. Their journeys are equally strange: they travel back and forth between the Ocean of the Depths and the Nimbus Sea. The Alphilan people are clearly involved somehow, but the mystery remains unsolved.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The coral reefs between Lumethia and Vaeloria, where Alphilan communities have settled, are home to axolotls with a passion for music and painting. Many Aquatic Whitenesses cross the Nimbus Sea to reach Abondance, where they appear to relish the city’s rich blend of cultures.

The great military fortress-city of Dragheïr is a dam between the ocean and the Blazing Sea, a place of exchange between Eltherians and Dhöggeïrs, and a city rich in symbols with a noble martial culture. Blaze is one of those symbols: a male mage who masters Water and Fire and represents the alliance between Hadeïr and Nordvinter. Legend says that one day, two heroes who oppose each other in every way will manage to free Hadeïr from the flames. They will purify Mount Vulcan and free the mother of the Dhöggeïr. Blaze is a wise, soothing figure.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Blue-Stone-Eater is a small dinosaur from the jungles of Presolda. Its eggs are incubated by the heat of the caves in southern Emeldarion. They survive alone or with their siblings and feed on ores and rocks of all kinds. Their adult form depends on their diet. Among those recorded are the Celestial Dragosaurs of Aelther and of the Dunes of Shal'Zaar. The latter are tamed as mounts by monster hunters.

The Drako'vish ranges stretch across the north of Lumethia. They form a border with Hadeïr, land of the Great Lions. This region suffered heavy corruption by Fire. The creatures touched and infected often have only one hope: the Blazing Willow of the Détwin woods. Catimimi was among the young infected lions. Barely saved by the Willow, he often tells the story of his king leading him to the woods. Catimimi witnessed the end of the battle between his kin. Today, he is tasked with protecting Leo.

Since the beginning of the pilgrimages, a cat similar to the imaginary panthers appears in the dreams of the Eltherians. It always indicates the location of the great sage of the sacred stone. The south of Lumethia is thus the starting point of every pilgrimage. At the start of these premonitory dreams, no one clearly understood the message. This feline appeared physically before those who ignored the call. It is in fact a request before it is a warning: the pilgrimage must be undertaken. The Olforgeurs, having heard the Eltherians speak of this cat, proposed to call it Catixy — a tribute to their Oniyx colleagues, gone since time immemorial.

Deep within Nyevielh’s dreadful Dreaming Forest dwells an Eternal corrupted by the abyssal power released when the Starry Sea fractured. When your vision blooms with color, the river water seems drinkable, the grass feels comfortable, and the air becomes breathable—run! Your life depends on it. Do not stop to question this forest: if any protocol has been left for the unfortunate souls who dare enter, follow its instructions.

Abyssal monsters possess indescribably horrific forms. These demonic creatures were encountered during the Oniyx expedition, a terrifying venture into the depths of the temple of Zaar’Phahl in Shal’Zaar. A deep unease accompanied the group’s progress through the Abyss. Though their senses were deceived at every turn, they eventually made out a crystal of pure energy. The rare discovery was nothing more than a crude trap set by a monster. The Abyssal gleefully slaughtered nearly a quarter of the group before growing bored.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Polychrome Owl is an emblematic animal of southern Vaeloria. In the woods, its hunt can be recognized by a peculiar sound reminiscent of a casino roulette wheel. Its feathers, collected from the ground each morning, are used to stuff pillows said to bring good fortune. The presence of a Polychrome Owl in a nearby wood means that the forest is healthy, making the species highly valued by the Vaelorians.

Abondance hosts a great many historical paintings. Among them is the Codex of Ancient Woes. The Kings who sealed the divinities are held responsible. Their action is a curse that contributed to the release of the Abyss. The event gave rise to a grim period called the Curse of the Kings. Today, we know they in fact played only a tragic role on a vast chessboard. This hateful painting was remade by the Mistress of Tints in disagreement with the artist. According to her, one must pay tribute to the forgotten heroes. The codex is an international topic of conversation.

Abondance hosts a great many paintings. Among them is the freshly painted Codex of Luminous Spells. The Kings who sealed the divinities are held responsible. Their action is a curse that contributed to the release of the Abyss. The event gave rise to a grim period called the Curse of the Kings. Today, we know they in fact played only a tragic role on a vast chessboard. This benevolent painting is a reconstruction of the Ancient Woes, remade by the Mistress of Tints. According to her, one must pay tribute to the forgotten heroes.

These days, in the wild lands of northern Emeldarion, lives a shamanic people led by the sage Keria. This people cultivates plants and raises animals, all bound to and nourished by the element of fire. Many training courses from the Dragheïr military academy are held in this region. Their purpose is to teach an understanding of the element of fire. Gerz, a former commando, retired here. A friend of the military school's headmistress, he agreed to welcome the students onto his ranch so they could be trained.

Somewhere out in the desert lands of Shal'Zaar, a powerful bull-like creature seems to be on the hunt. Its mere presence sends most monster hunters running. Some, frozen by the terror of the beast's aura, say the Abyssal simply ignored them and kept heading elsewhere. Tokscyth researchers tracked its path — a full loop around the continent. It's a worrying sign, should this thing ever find what it hunts so tirelessly.

After the single continent cracked apart, a gigantic inner sea formed, dotted with many islands. Some are held aloft by an unknown force above the Nimbus Sea. Others are true islands, made inaccessible by the presence of Abyssals. The Toad of the Stars is one of these monsters. With a single echoing croak, entire crews of sailors fall asleep. Those least fit to fight in the dream world are devoured. At the risk of becoming a fly at a giant toad's dinner, Nyevielh has been made inaccessible because of the danger of Toad of the Stars appearing.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Verdant Fruit Cruncher is a herbivore from Vaeloria that loves barely-ripe fruit fallen to the ground. Usually pretty inactive, its belly lets it stock up reserves for times when fruit is scarce — though sometimes they're found raiding food storehouses in the cold season.

Nyevielh’s dreadful Dreaming Forest is home to nightmarish mutations of the local fauna, spawned by the abyssal power released when the Starry Sea fractured. Beware of large bushes: Devourers of Fauna may be hiding within, waiting to ambush their prey. Do not stop to question this forest: if any protocol has been left for the unfortunate souls who dare enter, follow its instructions.

Making the great pilgrimage to the summit of the Celestial Mount is now the norm. Every pilgrim who succeeds is welcomed, beyond the clouds, by an Eternal who acknowledges their hard work and rewards their achievement. A rare few have claimed to have met the Calamity of light, Sky Dragon. The blessing of these people is proof enough of the truth of their words. This possibility led to the making of a great ground fresco in Abondance.

At the heart of Mount Vulcan lived a powerful Dhöggeïr. Its nest became the foundation of Logaïr’s first structures, and the great Forge City gradually grew under its protection. A bond of trust developed between the creature and the successive Fire Kings. Each King taught the Dhöggeïr language to his heir so that the new ruler could communicate with it in turn. No one knows what became of the creature after the corruption of Fire, but Hadeïr’s condition bodes ill. Many believe it took the form of an Abyssal Dragon.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, which nightmares then purify. Eternal agents patrol the Abyss to keep their shifting state stable. The Wyrmling of Lights handles the content of the dreams in the dream world. It creates the exchanges between the body and the subconscious of the Awakened. This complex process is said to allow the creation of new souls. Certain flaws suggest it doesn't do its job well.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. Incredible creatures inhabit the Lonely Isles, a cluster of flying islands above the Nimbus Sea. Among these species is the Celestial Dragosaur. Its nests can be observed on the cliffs of the continent of Aelther. Once adults, they head to the floating islands. No one knows why they go there, for now.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The masked Foxes, faithful to the King of Shadow, have settled in the mountains east of Nyevielh. These trained creatures wear a mask as a sign of loyalty. They face the abyssals prowling around their territory. This region is too cold for many Eltherians to live there. But the canine guardians of the Gleam of the White Fox ensure their safety.

Abondance hosts great many paintings. Among them is the astral whale Ephial. The painting on the ground is the subject of debate. The Mistress of Tints uses the whole city as her blank canvas, drawing many visitors. Ephial is her most striking painting. Some think it's a depiction of the pilgrimage — pilgrims identify with it in their quest for their Eternal at the Celestial Mount. Others think it's linked to the flying creature southwest of Emeldarion. The Mistress of Tints, for her part, stays discreet about the origin of her ideas.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. On the northern coasts of Hadeïr, you can see flaming jellyfish flying all the way to the center of the Blazing Sea. Their hot body allows their ascent before falling slowly back into the water. Underwater, they store up heat to begin their weekly cycle again. The Ignited Lizards, imported from Emeldarion, and the Medusine Thorns create a grand nighttime spectacle that is a source of national pride and the theme of many festivals.

After the single continent shattered, the environment struggled to regain its balance because elemactive activity remained far too intense after the divine wars. The Eternal, wrongly nicknamed Spirit of the Fauna, took on a role of regulation. It sees to the needs of the living species on the Surface. Meeting it is exceedingly rare, unless you're its target. Be careful not to disturb it in its work. It knows how to punish poachers without the slightest mercy, through its powerful abilities.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the Water Spirit spends whole days slowing the advance of the ice of the Crystal Lands. Active in a huge lake of Nordvinter, it is the only clearly visible spirit accessible to a large population. This peculiarity never fails to attract many travelers. However, disturbing a spirit's activity has a price that Lycaria, Shadow of the White, is ready to make one pay, so that no one bothers the little aquatic canine.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the Fire Spirit spends whole days calming the fiery imbalance of Hadeïr. Valiant and full of energy, it roams the fire elemactive zones — zones it tirelessly puts out, no doubt to preserve the elemental balance. It has been glimpsed on rare occasions with the soldiers of Dragheïr. Witnesses speak of a canine form where no one would dare set foot.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the light spirit spends whole days guiding pilgrims to the Celestial Mount of Aelther. Its social nature with the pilgrims makes it the perfect mascot. Before the great ascent, on the paths and in the villages of Okaemi, the pilgrims are always delighted to look after it. It can sometimes be seen intimidating those who break the rules of the continent.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the nature spirit spends whole days fighting against Fanure. Today, it tries to protect the Meridia from withering. This great tree of life is the symbol of Vaeloria. The spirit toils in the unfathomable depths of its roots. Its barks can sometimes be heard in this chaotic labyrinth. The few adventurers who brave the Roots are regularly exposed to elemactive zones. These seem to be erased by the passing of the canine, marking out a new path.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the shadow spirit spends whole days hunting the nightmares of Nyevielh. Its violent and dreadful activity has given it a most hostile appearance; the few Eltherians still alive prefer not to cross its path, for its prey is never far. A wooden statue was built in its honor at Port Rhyezeal, maintained there as a protective idol of Nyevielh and a scarecrow against abominations.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the earth spirit spends its days fighting in the corrupted desert of Shal'Zaar. Always on the move, it keeps the mines stocked with materials and battles the Abyssals. You can still see the marks of some of its long fights. A few monster hunters were lucky enough to catch it in action, and love to tell of their battle alongside the brave sand wolf.

Faerylia was renowned as the most learned and cultivated person in Shal’Zaar. A vassal of the Earth King, she mastered magic and the written word like no one else. Alone, she succeeded in deciphering the Primordial Codex. Time revealed, however, that she had disclosed only a fraction of the grimoire’s true contents. She explained precisely how to seal the Deities, from forging the runic weapons to constructing the portal. After attempting to claim powers akin to those of the Deities, she was punished with the destruction of her homeland. The Weaver of Chaos is now the world’s most wanted witch.

Abondance, the economic capital of Emeldarion, is as rich in natural resources as it is in culture. The full diversity of its population can be seen there. Yet choosing to live in this divided city is no easy matter. Often poorly informed, residents find themselves in need of help. Several companies control the area, and the most prosperous hold seats on the city’s ruling council. Clans such as the Wandering Feline form in the hope of gaining influence. This one welcomes Anthropomorphs, gives them guidance, and provides them with housing.

After the Light King abandoned Aelther, flowers with healing potential began to grow on the Celestial Mount. Some pilgrims pick them despite the bans and fail to complete their pilgrimage — but it lets them heal a loved one or earn a living in Abondance. The greatest of the Flowers of Life sits atop the highest mountain. It is made of gigantic petals and never opens. Everyone wonders what could be inside. Will a chosen one one day be able to open it? Is there a miracle remedy inside?

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. Along the western coasts of Lumethia, one can see clusters of algae coming from the Ocean of the Depths. These beaches are off-limits because of very aggressive Marineflowers that may have settled there. These sea eels are quite feared by fishermen. However, they are a delicacy, a specialty of the ports of Lumethia.

They say six children were born with a rune on their hand. In Nordvinter, within the great warrior tribe of the Nords, the chief's son Frost was born with strange animal features. Despite an ability to resist the cold, even the most intense, he endured much harassment. His parents' death gave him no more authority. It was only once his pilgrimage was complete that he was respected. Today, he is the master of the Dhöggeïr prince: Glacier. He is also the vice-president of the council of the Dragheïr military school. There he is recognized for his exploits.

History books recount this legend in many forms: the story of Aurelia, the Eternal who gave birth to the Pixarchs, and of her first creation, Gabriel. Both bound their fate to that of their people. Gabriel was a brilliant inventor and the closest friend of the Oniyx Lumisaros. Together, they created innovations that transformed everyday life, as well as legendary artifacts. The loss of the great winged beings during Aurelia’s Dawn is still mourned, although some survived the event, including the Nature King and Keria.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Green Guardian is a lizard deeply attached to its tree of life. When young, it leaves the nest to choose a shrub it will protect its whole life. It feeds on sap, plants and invasive insects. It helps the tree bud and spread its roots. The Green Guardian is native to Lumethia but was imported to Vaeloria and Emeldarion.

The corruption of Hadeïr by Fire is characterized by its Poison Gas. This powerful elemactive phenomenon drifts with the wind and causes countless afflictions. Creatures that come into contact with the mist are driven violently mad. Shadow and Fire cells then combine to create immortal abyssal creatures. The deadly haze originates at the heart of Mount Vulcan, where the Kings’ runic weapons were forged. Deposits recovered from the bottom of several bodies of water suggest an underground source. Analyses identify the substance as organic matter…

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Floral Giraffe is the pilgrims' favorite mount. They can grow crops on their Giraffe's coat within a few days. In Vaeloria, this noble animal provides a mobile vegetable garden available in all circumstances — any family worthy of the name owns its own Floral Giraffe.

Godlur was the first artificial creature designed by Gabriel and Lumisaros. It protected the Pixarch capital from the most belligerent Eternals. This powerful golem could harness photosynthesis to recharge its integrated Oniyx orbs, allowing it to operate by day or night. Many described it as indestructible. Is it still active somewhere? Could it still be operating at the heart of the Lonely Isles?

When the Fire King vanished, the peoples of Nordvinter heavily militarized to support Hadeïr. The Snow Warriors make the most of the extreme conditions — the continent's cold and the inner sea's heat — to build a fighting physique unmatched among the Eltherians. They are the pride of Dragheïr, and today's equivalent of the Light King's pack of old.

They say six children were born with a rune on their hand. In Shal'Zaar, in a village of monster hunters, a young girl can communicate with her mind. The moment she forms a link, her eyes seem filled with a purplish liquid. With her power, she tamed some of the most terrifying creatures of the Presolda jungle — tropical snakes and other dinosaurs that now aid monster hunters. For all these feats, she earned the title of Heraldess, a divine envoy echoing the vanished regent.

The Natus are a new tribal species made up of few individuals. They are very attached to their territory and seem to cultivate their own beliefs. Their superior intellect sets them apart from mere animals. In the Monts Nomades of Nordvinter, or in the scorching desert of Shal'Zaar, one can find very different ones and their villages. The Hibernatus of Nordvinter sometimes welcome freezing adventurers in exchange for stories.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The clear waters of the Nimbus Sea stretch along the southern shores of the new Vaeloria. The Nimbus Seahorse is the emblematic animal of this vast expanse. Males carry the fertilized eggs, while females protect both the males and their broods with their dorsal fins. The Alphilans use these creatures to signal their presence at the Surface. Ignoring that warning may provoke a dangerous and needless conflict.

As Vaeloria struggled to recover from the disappearance of the Nature King, the Sengo bandit clan terrorized the northwest. Ignea lived peacefully with her nomadic family until the day she hid from danger and watched the bandits slaughter everyone she loved. She then devoted her life to vengeance, training, and battle. While hunting the clan’s leader, she freed several villages and finally earned the duel to the death she had long sought. Despite her opponent’s countless underhanded schemes, she prevailed, took command of the clan, and transformed it into Vaeloria’s present-day adventurers’ guild.

These days, in the north of Emeldarion, magnificent ears of grain rise — the shoots of Bleh watered by the fire of the Flammeveilles. These fields are run with a master's hand by the shamans of Keria's tribe. Talking with her, you discover a strange Pixarch who doesn't hide her origins. She is equipped with Fire elemental catalysts, some of which alter her appearance. These illusions let her mask the scars of her past, she tells us. Very open to conversation, she offers her knowledge to anyone who wishes to drink it in. She soothes the tensions between the region's tribes with wisdom and altruism.

The Blades of the Forest were a people of Nymphs who protected the Pixarch woods. Often tasked with guarding a single tree or a forest clearing, they delighted in life’s simple pleasures and loved to play pranks. They were also fearsome warriors. No one knows whether their people still exist today. The Blades are believed to dwell within the Lonely Isles. Further research may reveal whether any members of their species survived.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, which nightmares then purify. Wander Blades is a painting depicting a confrontation with the Calamity of Shadow. In it, the Nightmare Reaper stands against the creature in Azeel’s Cemetery of the Void. Displayed in churches throughout the world, the work exalts duty and self-sacrifice in service of the common good.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Feathered Rabbits are among the easiest desert rodents to tame. They form a deep bond of trust with the desert tribes of Shal'Zaar. Able to sense danger like no other creature of the desert, and to fly, they are the ideal animal companion for a monster hunter. When a Feathered Rabbit panics, the Abyssals are never far away.

Around the lake of the Water Spirit, small rodents have made their home. The spirit companions play there and seem to communicate with butterflies. These curious little animals don't flee from Eltherians — quite the opposite. They've become a mascot of the northern mountainous region of Vaeloria. This peaceful ecosystem has found its balance far from any predator. These little furballs surely keep a secret deep in their burrows. But Lycaria makes sure no one disturbs the calm of the lake.

We have little information about Hadeïr beyond Dragheïr. We do know, however, that the Blazing Willow of Détwin Forest is an entity that must be protected. Able to cleanse creatures afflicted by corruption, it represents a source of hope for all of Hadeïr. Yet it cannot move and must be defended against the Abyssals. An Eltherian bastion was therefore established in the heart of the forest to keep them away from the saving entity. Dragons are the greatest known abyssal threat. In the region, some Dhöggeïrs attuned to Fire have become powerful corrupted Dragons. Repelling even one is nothing short of a miracle—and has already cost many soldiers their lives.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Carrier of Shal'Zaar, in the wild, is one of the few creatures able to stand against the desert's Abyssal threat. Its abilities make it a top pick to tame — for combat or for hauling goods. Monster hunters live in harmony with herds of Carriers.

The Drako'vish ranges stretch across the north of Lumethia. They form a border with Vaeloria and Hadeïr, land of the Great Lions. As the lions clashed in the northern savanna, Sylvan died in one final battle. Following the sacrifice of this shared friend, the clan leaders heeded his last wish and accepted peace. They then took Leo in. Despite a growing interest in the Eltherians who resemble him, Leo considers the Great Lions his family. He works to have them seen as a species in their own right, like the Natus.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. Thorn of Love is a hedgehog whose spines are said to be hallucinogenic — widely used in TOX research to reduce side effects. Few of these echidnas are still found in Vaeloria, but pilgrims report running into them along the way in Emeldarion and Aelther. Talks are underway to reintroduce the species to its natural habitat.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, which nightmares then purify. Eternal agents patrol the Abyss to keep their shifting state stable. The Leviathan of the Skies is one of them; it weaves the bubbles of each individual dream in its wake. Should it one day stop or disappear, the Awakened would be condemned to know only nightmare during their sleep.

Eternals devoted to the preservation of the Surface appeared after certain catastrophes. Their purpose is to keep the mistakes that were made from happening again. Protector of the ruins of a gigantic worksite of the past, the one they call the Eye of the Mountains can be observed not far from the Ether Falls, southwest of Emeldarion, or northwest of Shal'Zaar. Some pilgrims who have glimpsed it see a good omen in it. Others who have faced it are no longer here to tell of it.

The ancestral Oniyx species was led by a great chief known as the Inventor. His people vanished in rebellion against the divinities. The writings of Lumethia keep his courage and his many sacrifices in memory. Aided by his second, Lumisaros, the Inventor designed the magic orbs named after his species — still used today, though no one knows how to manufacture them, so they are looked after with care. He created many weapons and defenses against the divine madness of the old days. Today, his creations are prisoners of the crystal lands east of Nordvinter.

They say six children were born with a rune on their hand. In Dragheïr, the slums see many war orphans struggle to survive. This atrocious military meritocracy, beginning at the earliest age, gave rise to Lisa. As a child, she showed unmatched combat abilities as well as a mastery of the Dhöggeïr language. A noble family, that of Pyra, decided to adopt her for these feats. Her studies are funded, and she becomes president of the military academy's council.

The fight against Fire's corruption pits the inhabitants against many Abyssals. These creatures crawl out of the earth's bowels through the lava flows of Mount Vulcan. The Ignatius are powerful giant serpents. They prowl near the lava currents and multiply throughout Hadeïr. They block the passage of battalions and rival the powerful Dhöggeïr. Their scales are used to craft weapons and armor. Among these Ignatius, one alone is said to be the source of this invasion: a Logidrake, a priority target, with the hope of one day reaching Logaïr.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. North of Emeldarion, you can see these otters come down from the Crystal Lands, passing through Abondance before swimming back up the waterway to start their mad descent all over again. You can even see them, sometimes, clinging to orbs they bring up from the seabed — a strange behavior the Alphilans keep secret.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Glimmers of Hope are the only neutral creatures in Nyevielh’s forest. They are said to mark the path to Vladislaus’s manor, and their presence also means that no abyssal monster is nearby. Do not stop to question this forest: if any protocol has been left for the unfortunate souls who dare enter, follow its instructions.

After the single continent fractured, a gigantic inland sea formed, dotted with many islands. Some remain suspended above the Nimbus Sea by an unknown force; others are true islands made inaccessible by abyssal monsters. The Lightbearer is one of those creatures. Its glow draws passengers from their ships, and many are said to have thrown themselves into the water under the sway of its illusions. These dreadful monsters have forced several sea routes to close. Nyevielh remains inaccessible because Abyssal Lightbearers may appear at any time.

Lums is a renowned singer from Abondance. Her performances draw on her two personalities and her fascination with the Starry Sea; the stars and the ocean are her favorite themes. She began her career at the Katrobu bar, which also welcomed the Mistress of Tints. The two artists care for one another like sisters despite their differences. The singer’s next tour, “Thalassophobia,” is a sound-and-light show. On several songs, she will be accompanied by artwork from the Mistress of Tints. The tour appears to herald a major turning point in one of their careers.

Originally from the Lonely Isles, an anthropomorphic martial master carrying a metamorphosis artifact settled northwest of Emeldarion. Amphibian gave life to many of the village's inhabitants. This shamanic sanctuary then grew with Keria's help: in exchange for land, the reptilian used his staff to help Keria build up her fire tribe. Asked why he left the flying isles, he always answers that it's the story of a broken friendship — of diverging ideals he regrets more and more as time goes by.

The history books tell of a society in which each artisan specialized in a single trade, built on collective efficiency and trust in one's neighbor. The Olforgeurs are stocky beings, barely shorter than Eltherians and very broad-shouldered. They have always been associated with the Oniyx through a shared passion for craft. Master Blacksmith Thronebéur, is an Olforgeur legend. His story keeps alive, over a good drink, the memory of comrades fallen in battle. It also celebrates knowledge passed down through generations. He is said to have been a close friend of the great Oniyx chief.

They say that six children were born with a rune on their hand. In Abondance, in Katrobu’s pleasure district, the Nameless struggle to build a future for themselves. A rebellious young artist repaints entire sections of the city every day. Constantly pursued by the authorities, she nevertheless drew countless tourists with her work. The Mistress of Tints thus became a celebrity with followers throughout the world. She is said to have visions of her nightmares without ever experiencing ordinary dreams. She paints them to release them and preserve her mind.

Elther would not exist without the Deities; all life is the product of divine creation. The creators each have their own works and doctrines. The runic language used by these supreme beings is an incomprehensible score. Only the appearance of certain runes remains accessible to the inhabitants of the Surface. The Melody of Divinities is a religious chant that has crossed the ages. The work gives thanks to the divine. The chant's incomprehensible psalms are studied to better understand the text.

The woods of Azeel stretch northwest of Vaeloria and are home to non-aggressive creatures whose sole purpose seems to be frightening visitors. Bouha has therefore become a tourist destination famed for its tests of courage. These trials are staged by the Forest Accomplices, the most imposing of whom is the Alphilan Moxilys. Each visitor follows a personalized route through the woods. No one knows why the service is free, a secret concealed behind wordless humming. Moxilys is an emblematic figure in the village of Alween and accompanies every brave challenger with a song.

The many deposits of Poison Gas in the Blazing Sea turned its depths black as oil. Without the introduction of Scorch to Dragheïr, the pollution would have spread and rendered the forge unusable. During their pilgrimages, young people from Nordvinter sometimes encounter a mound of putrid flesh and rock soaked in a viscous substance. These many-polyped creatures cannot move. Mindless and carried by the winds, they pose no direct threat to the city. Abyssal Galleys nevertheless represent a grave danger to anyone crossing the Blazing Sea.

Since time immemorial, the Dhöggeïr are born from great eggs high up in the mountains. These legendary creatures are the arbiters of the battles between Eternals, protecting the Surface. Aldrin and Emeraldoth are the firstborn. They have often disagreed, though brothers from the same egg. As the single continent found itself fragmented, the two protected the living with the full extent of their powers. Southern Vaeloria was renamed Emeldarion in their honor. Aldrin is said to have found rest on the Lonely Isles, and his brother in the Marais'Cage of Emeldarion.

Abyssal monsters have an indescribably horrific form. These demonic creatures were encountered during the Oniyx expedition — a horrifying venture into the depths of the temple of Zaar'Phahl in Shal'Zaar. The group's progress through the Abyss was grueling. Some members saw their belongings and provisions stolen — resources essential to their survival. At laughter that seemed to come from every direction, the invisible creature reveled in the situation; some scattered belongings, however, seemed to leave it uninterested. The journey grew ever more horrifying as hunger increased. Some began to eat what they never should have, continuing to feed the morbid curiosity of their stalker. The story of the Nakyel is told in Shal'Zaar to remind that curiosity is a nasty flaw.

Among the Eternals, Spirits, and other mythical beings is Neilla. This singular entity creates currents and keeps the waters from overflowing. Those who follow the currents may glimpse the demigoddess for the briefest instant. Countless sailors, captivated by her beauty and her secrets, have set out in search of the beautiful Alphilan. Yet the most dangerous routes spare not even the boldest travelers. After so many ships and lives were lost, a treaty was enacted forbidding the use of vessels to hunt the Lady.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Hatchlings of Midas are said to be the offspring of the Glimmers of Hope. It hasn't yet been proven, due to the difficulty of Aelther's restrictions — its fauna and flora are hard to observe. Their nest is perched high, at the height of the tallest trees. They only become visible during the ascent of the Celestial Mount, when the summit comes to eye level.

According to many historical accounts, the war between the higher magical species and the Eternals was raging. Armed with their finest weaponry, blending elemental magic and weapons of mass destruction, the Oniyx bought the time needed to seal the Deities. The most fearsome machine, Paguroniyx, was piloted by the Inventor. No one knows where this machine is today. Perhaps trapped in the ice of the crystal lands? Or maybe it sank into the ocean depths?

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Imaginary Panther teleports through spatial rifts similar to Vivy's. These rifts are traced toward the arrival point by one of the eyes present on its body. It is sometimes found on the beaches of Vaeloria, where it lets itself be observed. It seems to commute there from the Lonely Isles. The panther is neutral, even though its appearance suggests an elemental corruption.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. Some shallow areas of the Ocean are in fact the domain of a giant octopus. These octopuses, non-aggressive toward the ships of Lumethia, are nonetheless territorial. Their tentacles come out of the water to emit an alert sound signaling the octopus's presence. Ships that ignore the warning end up at the bottom of the sea. Only one accident is on record, dating from the old days. Today, these creatures serve as landmarks at sea to chart routes.

Meridia is today a prosperous city. The council handles foreign diplomatic relations. It is the only country lucky enough to trade with the Alphilans. The princess, named after the sacred tree, Meridia, took a great interest in the sea folk. On the southern coasts, she met the wounded Lord of the Tides. She cared for him and there they cultivated their love. Their bond created a relationship between the two peoples. Today, the warrior Princess leads at the front alongside her husband. She is a new hope against the Abyssals of the Starry Sea.

Many accounts mention the peoples of old, including an ancestral species of small humanoids with feline features. Now extinct, we keep their courage and sacrifice in memory. In the fight against the Eternals, all the Oniyx communities created an entity of controlled chaos: the Prisoner of the Machine. Struck by such a weapon, an Eternal is sealed within the sphere. Made essentially of magic, a prisoner is kept in a state of deep sleep. Its regenerative capacity becomes an inexhaustible source of energy — still powering the autonomy of the Oniyx factories, trapped in the ice of the Crystal Lands.

Abyssal monsters have an indescribably horrific form. These demonic creatures were encountered during the Oniyx expedition — a horrifying venture into the depths of the temple of Zaar'Phahl in Shal'Zaar. Once the group's descent into the Abyss was over, the survivors hurried to seal off the temple's excavation site. A massive fortification was set up so no Abyssal could get out. An artificial Oniyx creature was built alongside it — a powerful, immense creation that now guards nothing but ruins.

As the corruption spread within the walls of the city of Logaïr, Pyro, the greatest aviator of his time and loyal vassal of the Fire King, saw to the evacuation of the uninfected civilians. The history books tell of those final moments, which today make him one of the great saving figures within Dragheïr. As he began his painful abyssal transformation, he sealed the gates of the city of the forges before him. Cursed today alongside his King, Pyro, in the fearsome form of a phoenix, still dwells in the city now renamed the infernal city.

Abyssal monsters have an indescribably horrific form. These demonic creatures were encountered during the Oniyx expedition — a horrifying venture into the depths of the temple of Zaar'Phahl in Shal'Zaar. The group's progress through the Abyss was grueling. Some members saw bright red eyes appear on their skin. No one knows what could have caused this phenomenon; perhaps a contamination. Consumed by murderous urges, they became dangerous, hyperactive zombies. This plague was named "Raffteru", the boundary of the abyss — the law that governs the corruption of the living in these lands and forbids their existence.

Death does not exist in Elther. In the Abyss, the dreams and nightmares of the Awakened mingle to purge damned souls: dreams shape new souls, while nightmares cleanse them of their regrets. Not every creature accepts this system. The Regent of the Abyss is a powerful member of the Logidrake family, serpentine abominations capable of commanding hordes of Abyssals. They wreak havoc across the world with alarming coordination. This one was sighted south of Shal’Zaar and appears to be responsible for the Abyssals that have risen to the Surface.

Not all Tokscyth are just alchemists. Some care more about the thrill of adventure. They contribute a great deal to their kin's research: their knowledge of plants, ores and mushrooms helped create TOX — a substance with random effects that are not always without consequences. The adventurers of this species are small, fearless daredevils from Hadeïr, braving mountains and seas in search of the very best for their creations.

The Drako’vish ranges stretch across northern Lumethia, forming a border with Vaeloria, land of the Great Lions. Faced with a powerful wave of Fire corruption, the King of the Blazing Flames and his clan were forced to seek new lands. He had no choice but to move his subjects onto Aurora’s territory. His body, corrupted by Fire, took on the appearance of an Eltherian. Aurora denied him any land, igniting a violent war. The two clans fought for days in the savanna of northern Lumethia. The conflict ended with the tragic death of Sylvan, a friend to both sides.

The title of elemental King is honorary, but carries immense responsibility for maintaining elemental balance. The Kings equipped their heirs with runic weapons. According to Faerylia’s interpretation of the Primordial Codex, those weapons would allow them to seal the Deities and win their freedom. The King of Water, a nomadic merchant, had the tradition of teaching a disciple about the waters and the markets. The last heir, husband of the Alphilan queen, is reported missing along with his wife; the trail leads back to the Crystal Lands.

The title of elemental King is honorary, but carries immense responsibility for maintaining elemental balance. The Kings equipped their heirs with runic weapons. According to Faerylia’s interpretation of the Primordial Codex, those weapons would allow them to seal the Deities and win their freedom. The Fire King's title was passed down hereditarily. The weapon and the key to the Forge City are then entrusted to the younger heir. The last heir and his son Aidan sacrificed themselves against the fire corruption of Hadeïr.

The title of elemental King is honorary, but carries immense responsibility for maintaining elemental balance. The Kings equipped their heirs with runic weapons. According to Faerylia’s interpretation of the Primordial Codex, those weapons would allow them to seal the Deities and win their freedom. The Kings of shadow and light had a diplomatic relationship. The cracking of the single continent created a clean break between the two heirs. Aelther was abandoned by the heir of light. He left behind only pilgrimage markers.

Being the King of an element is an honorary title. It signifies a high responsibility in the elemental balance. The Kings had their heirs equipped with a runic weapon. However, the only King without an heir is the King of Nature. This Pixarch, his wings mysteriously torn off, bound himself to the weapon. In keeping with the texts of the Primordial Codex according to Faerylia, these weapons would make it possible to seal the Deities and win freedom. He reigned over Vaeloria for centuries. When the disease of Fanure appeared, he gave his life creating the Meridia.

The title of elemental King is honorary, but carries immense responsibility for maintaining elemental balance. The Kings equipped their heirs with runic weapons. According to Faerylia’s interpretation of the Primordial Codex, those weapons would allow them to seal the Deities and win their freedom. The Kings of shadow and light had a diplomatic relationship. The cracking of the single continent created a clean break between the two heirs. Nyevielh became a hostile zone, forcing the heir of Shadow into perpetual combat. These cursed lands are an open-air nightmare that one should never visit.

The title of elemental King is honorary, but carries immense responsibility for maintaining elemental balance. The Kings equipped their heirs with runic weapons. According to Faerylia’s interpretation of the Primordial Codex, those weapons would allow them to seal the Deities and win their freedom. The Earth King was a herald and spokesman for the Eternals, Phahl'Aon of Shal'Zaar — the richest and most advanced expanse of the old days. When the kingdom fell, he vanished without a trace.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. Cloudy Rodents live on the clouds of the Celestial Mount, which they devour like cotton candy. Native to the Eternals’ Celestial Realms, where they are considered an invasive species, they sometimes cross the sky aboard cumulonimbus clouds that have drifted away from their realm.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Golden Boar is part of the wildlife living in the forests of Aelther. It's mostly found at the foot of the Celestial Mount, where it feeds on gold and roots. This diet strengthens its gold-rich skeleton and makes it quite dangerous to provoke. Pilgrims have a rule to feed only on Honey Caterpillars there. That way, the continent's species are protected from poaching.

In the great forge of Logaïr, gigantic creatures churned the lava of Mount Vulcan. The unique work of the Minions of Flames — which no one could replicate at such temperatures — made the craftsmanship of Hadeïr prosperous and essential. Outside of Oniyxia, it was the Oniyx's favorite city. Many Olforgeurs worked the materials alongside passionate artisans. Without the Minions of Flames, the runic weapons could never have been forged. They made Logaïr the finest forge in the world in its time.

These days, a shamanic people led by the sage Keria live in the wild lands of northern Emeldarion. They cultivate plants and raise animals, all attuned to and nourished by the element of Fire. Scorch are small igneous lizards that help preserve the aquatic ecosystem. They feed on pollutants found in the water, whether mineral or plant-based. The lizards dry them inside their large mouths, then burn them in their stomachs. This unusual digestive process can cause fiery burps.

Abyssal monsters possess indescribably horrific forms. These demonic creatures were encountered during the Oniyx expedition, a terrifying venture into the depths of the temple of Zaar’Phahl in Shal’Zaar. While seeking a way out of the Abyss, the group encountered new abyssal scourges. Their forms were difficult to describe, but after their initial fright, the explorers realized that these monstrosities were pointing them toward the exit. Trusting them was their last hope. These unlikely guides mowed down monsters like wheat, wielding weapons fed by the elemental chaos of the place. The specters thus kept the Abyss from spilling onto the Surface, giving the survivors time to raise fortifications around the breach. They were named “Shado,” from shadow without its W: as the initial of win, that letter had no place in an endless battle where victory could never be achieved. The temple of Zaar’Phahl is adorned with countless decorations in their honor.

East of Emeldarion lives a very territorial martial tribe. The little we know of them are strong wolf motifs. Lightning seems to strike their region constantly. Researchers believe the Light King and his descendants may have settled there. The theory has never been confirmed. A spatial rift always opens before anyone who crosses the line of the canine totems. Vivy always appears first, followed by her Radiant Shinobi — a masked and visibly overtrained battalion.

The Pixarch disappearance left the Anthropomorphs with a heavy legacy. The Astral Healer is proof of the survival of the protectors of the Tree of Mysteries. She can be encountered in the forest of Vaelor. She is searching for "Gabriel's staff", an artifact capable of metamorphosis, stolen after an internal conflict that cost the Samouraï Croc his life. As she was away during the Fanure epidemic, she had entrusted the staff to her second, who lost it in single combat. All she knows about the culprit is that he is probably somewhere in Vaeloria.

These days, in the wild lands of northern Emeldarion, lives a shamanic people led by the sage Keria. This people cultivates plants and raises animals, all bound to and nourished by the element of fire. Many training courses from the Dragheïr military academy are held in this region. The Pyrokinetic Sorceress, headmistress of this prestigious school, sought a way to train her students against the fire corruption. She then reached an agreement with Keria.

These days, a shamanic people led by the sage Keria live in the wild lands of northern Emeldarion. They cultivate plants and raise animals, all attuned to and nourished by the element of Fire. Some of these animals received the blessing of the metamorphosis staff. Transformed into Anthropomorphs, the Wheat Mice now help the village function. These exceptional farmers guarantee the flawless quality of the Bleh and keep other animals and crows from damaging the crops.

The world’s creators have no form that can be described; they are likely divine instruments. Their apocalyptic appearances throughout history nevertheless earned them the name Calamities. Once their work—creative and destructive in equal measure—was complete, the Calamities withdrew into the Abyss. There they lie dormant, separating the material world from the realm of dreams. The Sovereign of the Ether Falls is a gigantic serpentine creature. Bursting from the waters of the Abyss, it shattered the single continent into countless fragments. This event is known as the Great Cataclysm.

The world's creators have no describable form; they are probably divine tools. But their historical appearance with apocalyptic features earned them the name of Calamities. Their work — as much creative as destructive — complete, the Calamities reside in the Abyss where, dormant, they separate the material world from the dream world. The Sovereign of Flames is a gigantic creature of serpentine form, similar to the Ignatius. In Hadeïr, the Eltherians hold it responsible for the Fire's corruption.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. In the region of Azeel, whose woods stretch across the lands northwest of Vaeloria, one can find non-aggressive creatures whose goal is to scare. The Bouha thus becomes a tourist spot for its tests of courage, or for its Canine Specter. It takes the form of the last animal companion you loved, letting you say goodbye to it one last time.

In Elther, it's normal to be afraid to sleep, as the slightest dream or nightmare can change an entire life. These dreamlike depictions are haunted by various premonitory apparitions. The Emissary of Nightmares is a powerful saving creature. It appears on the most dreadful and deadly nights. It saves sleepers from an otherwise inevitable death. Often accompanied by a message, the creature introduces itself as Squall.

The Drako’vish ranges stretch across northern Lumethia, forming a border with Vaeloria, land of the Great Lions. During a journey devoted to his research, Sylvan took in an abandoned child named Leo. When he learned that a bloody war had broken out between his childhood friends, Catimimi urged him to intervene and end the fighting. Sylvan brought about the long-awaited truce, but suffered mortal wounds in the process. With his final words, he asked that Leo be cared for. His sacrifice ended the war.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Weavers of Words inhabit the tropical jungle of Presolda, southeast of Emeldarion. They rank among the region’s greatest animal threats. These giant spiders imitate the cries of prey to lure in their predators. Once caught in the spiders’ webs, those predators become stores of food.

In the region of Azeel, whose woods stretch northwest of Vaeloria, one can find non-aggressive creatures whose simple goal is to scare. The Bouha thus becomes a tourist spot for its tests of courage. The trial there is watched over by the Nocturnal Watcher. If a visitor panics dangerously, this powerful owl appears. It brings people back to a safe zone. It also speaks the common tongue very well. Its magical power carries a heavy secret that it will never reveal.

With the single continent freshly shattered, the environmental imbalance couldn't easily right itself — because of far too much elemactive activity in the aftermath of the divine war. The Eternal Verdelune took on a role of regulation. It sees to the needs of the growing plants on the Surface. Meeting it is exceedingly rare and heralds good harvests. Be careful not to disturb it in its work — its disappearance, they say, would wither the crops and pollute the waters.

East of Emeldarion lives a very territorial martial tribe. The little we know of them are strong wolf motifs. Lightning seems to strike their region constantly. Researchers believe the Light King and his descendants may have settled there. The theory has never been confirmed. A spatial rift always opens before anyone who crosses the line of the canine totems. Vivy always appears first. Followed by her Shinobi, she threatens to attack anyone who would go further into the lands of the Pack.

Treasurer of Nyevielh, Vladislaus handled most of the documents for his regent. A renowned philosopher and researcher, he is the childhood friend of the Kings of Earth and Shadow. As nightmares made his lands uninhabitable, he was entrusted with fragments of the Codex. Vladislaus had a manor built with moving rooms — impossible to get around without following precise patterns. The duchess and some servants chose to follow him. The Codex has been heavily protected from nightmares for centuries. No one knows what became of them... Are they still alive?

In the Crystal Lands east of Nordvinter, humanoids accompanied by wolves have been spotted on multiple occasions. These travelers of the icy peaks seem to be scouting the frozen zone. They have already attacked several worksites aiming to free the Oniyx technologies from the ice. Since then, no one dares try again, on pain of reprisals. They seem peaceful toward the youths of Nordvinter searching for their Dhöggeïr. Nothing is known of their origin. Their esoteric equipment suggests they come from Emeldarion.

Historical accounts tell us the Oniyx were not only inventors. Some used their intelligence to set off on adventure. The most famous was Lumisaros, incapable of staying put on a chair. In charge of developing Oniyxia's relations, he was part of an adventuring group known as the deviants. Wibs, nicknamed "l'enflammée", is one of them, born with a rare elemental affinity for her species. Adventuring at sea was one of her greatest dreams. She built ships to cross the ocean with Lumisaros's help. Those gigantic machines now sit in the port of Lumethia. The painting of the happy Oniyx hangs in every captain's cabin. Wibs is celebrated every year with a festival of laughter and songs all across the port.

Now that the world seems to have regained its elemental balance, nature and its adaptation to the environment can be observed as never before. The Wyrms are a hostile fauna of the Shal'Zaar regions. Somewhere between a snake and a sandworm, these enormous creatures turn sand into crystal. The mines created by their activity are called Horned Dunes. Learning to avoid and to fight them is daily life in the Shal'Azd'Hun region. Crystals are a rare and precious resource for monster hunters — their purity allows any element to be inserted into them.

Sir Leafguard is a Nymph in the service of the Dhöggeïr Emeraldoth. Since the latter isn't the most eloquent, Yotaru served as his messenger and interpreter. Brave and warm-hearted, he sacrificed much of himself to meet the needs of his lizard friend. Today, in the Marais'Cage south of Emeldarion, he makes sure pilgrims respect the area's rules. No one may leave the road or set foot on the ground. Guided by such a living legend, the pilgrims gladly comply.

They say six children were born with a rune on their hand. In Shal'Zaar, among the dunes, the hunter tribes prepare their hunts. To defend the children and non-combatants, the most gifted teenagers are trained day and night. Among them is Zayd, a warrior whose strength defies the laws of physics. The young man can multiply his muscular density. However, he burns huge amounts of energy and needs to eat a lot — so he's responsible for his own meals. Once he finally reached adulthood, an important figure of the desert came to take him in as a disciple.

Long ago, Gabriel and Lumisaros built a mysterious tree within the Pixarch capital. The tree could reclaim surplus elemactive energy to cleanse the environment. Today, the ruins are fragmented into a flying archipelago above the Nimbus Sea. These Lonely Isles are a dream expedition for researchers. The tree is theorized to be responsible for the appearance of Floral Zombies — humanoid in form and in a vegetative state. They fall a few at a time from the heights of the islands and are washed onto the coasts of Vaeloria. They are weak abyssal monsters and an excellent subject of study.
